title: FEI Tribunal Decision — Final Decision Settlement Agreement  C26-0002 2025 BS06 GABOR DE FLORYS (MANDILLE)
text:
DECISION RENDERED BY THE FEI TRIBUNAL
11 February 2026
In the matter of
FÉDÉRATION EQUESTRE INTERNATIONALE (the “FEI”)
vs.
Ms Astrid MANDILLE – Person Responsible (the “PR”)
together the “Parties”
(Reference No. FEI Tribunal: C26-0002 MANDILLE)
COMPOSITION OF THE FEI TRIBUNAL PANEL:
Ms Harveen Thauli (CAN), Sole Panel Member
FEI Case number: 2025/BS06 GABOR DE FLORYS
Horse/Passport: GABOR DE FLORYS/109FJ44/FRA
Person Responsible/ID/NF: Astrid MANDILLE/10349599/FRA
Event/Date: Pony Measuring Session, Ludon-Médoc, France
Date of sample collection: 28.04.2025
Prohibited Substance(s): Bromazepam
Bar Code No.: 1608996
1

All the words used in this Final Decision beginning with a capital letter and not previously
defined have the meaning set forth in the specific definitions of the FEI General Regulations
(the “GRs”) and Statutes, the FEI Veterinary Regulations (the “VRs”), the 2025 Equine
Prohibited Substance List (the “FEI Prohibited List”), and the Equine Anti-Doping and
Controlled Medication Regulations (the “EADCMRs”). The Equine Anti-Doping Rules (the
“EAD Rules”) and the Equine Controlled Medication Rules (the “ECM Rules”) are set out in
the EADCMRs.
I. Introduction
1. This Final Decision pertains to the FEI case, 2025/BS06 GABOR DE FLORYS. In this
matter, the FEI notified the PR that a violation of Article 2.1 (The Presence of a Banned
Substance and/or its Metabolites or Markers in a Horse’s Sample) and Article 2.2 (the
Use of a Banned Substance and/or Banned Method) of the EAD Rules had occurred
based on the positive finding of Bromazepam in the Sample of the horse, Gabor de
Florys (the “Horse”), which was collected when the Horse was presented for Pony
Measurement in Ludon-Médoc (France) on 28 April 2025 (the “Event”).
2. The FEI and the PR agreed to a Settlement Agreement on 26 January 2026 (the
“Settlement Agreement”). The Settlement Agreement together with the attached
Exhibits are hereby incorporated by reference in this Final Decision.
II. Applicable Rule Provisions
3. The following regulations are applicable to the present case:
Statutes 25th edition, effective 21 November 2023 (the “Statutes”).
General Regulations, 24thedition, 1 January 2020, updates effective 1 January 2025.
(the “GRs”).
Internal Regulations of the FEI Tribunal, 4th Edition, 1 February 2025 (the “IRs”).
FEI Equine Anti-Doping and Controlled Medication Regulations, 4th edition, effective
1 January 2025 (the “EADCMRs”). As only the EAD Rules apply in the present case,
reference will be made hereinafter only to this second chapter of the EADCMRs.
FEI Veterinary Regulations, 15th edition 2023, effective 1 January 2025 (the “VRs”).
2

III. Factual background and initial proceedings
4. Ms Astrid MANDILLE (FEI ID 10349599) is the Horse’s owner, and the PR in
accordance with Article 118.3 of the GRs.
5. The FEI is the IOC-recognised international governing body for the equestrian sport
disciplines of Dressage and Para-Dressage, Jumping, Eventing, Driving and Para-
Driving, Endurance and Vaulting.
6. The PR is a member of the French Equestrian Federation (the “FRA-NF”), the latter
being a member of the FEI. The PR is therefore bound by the EAD Rules.
7. The Horse was tested during the Event and returned a positive finding of
Bromazepam, which is an anxiolytic used in the treatment of anxiety and insomnia.
Bromazepam is classified as a Banned Substance, prohibited at all times, under the
FEI Prohibited List.
8. Therefore, the positive findings of Bromazepam in the Sample gave rise to a
violation of the EAD Rules (the “EAD Rule Violation”).
9. The FEI informed the PR of the EAD Rule Violation in a notification letter dated 2 June
2025 (the “Notification Letter”). In accordance with Article 7.4.1. of the EAD Rules,
the FEI provisionally suspended the PR as at the date of the Notification Letter (the
“Provisional Suspension”).
10. The PR had the right to request an analysis of the B Sample. The PR did not request
its analysis; therefore, she irrevocably waived this right.
11. In the Notification Letter, the FEI further informed the PR of her right to provide an
explanation within 20 days from the date of the Notification Letter.
12. The PR provided statements to the FEI where she explained how the Prohibited
Substance entered the Horse’s system. The Horse, owned by the PR since 2022, is
a pony stallion. The Horse is reluctant to compete and stops at the entrance of the
arena, rearing up (a behaviour the Horse had already displayed before the PR
purchased him). After the purchase, the Horse spent two years in the pasture
without any work. The PR hoped that, after this period of rest, he would be willing
to resume competing over small 90 cm obstacles, but this has not been the case. In
February 2025, the PR signed an agreement with a third party, whereby the Horse
would be loaned to said third party, free of charge, for the purpose of breeding
(inseminating) a mare. Under this agreement, the Horse was moved to a Chateau,
where he lived in the same paddock as the mare. The PR decided to bring the Horse
3

to the Pony Measuring Session because it was held very close to the Chateau, and
she believed that having an official measurement certificate would be useful for the
potential approval of the Horse as a breeding stallion. Following receipt of the
Notification Letter, the PR inquired with the mare’s owner about the source of the
Prohibited Substance. The owner explained that the mare is a pony suffering from
behavioural disorders and that he had administered Regumate (Altrenogest) and
Lexomil (Bromazepam) to her. The mare was under treatment when the Horse was
at the Chateau. The PR submitted a veterinary prescription document issued on 7
January 2025 certifying that the mare was diagnosed with hormone-dependent
behavioural disorders. The prescription includes the oral administration of
Regumate (1 dose per 400 kg, once per day for six months), as well as Lexomil 6 mg
(4 tablets per day for a period of 6 to 8 months). The two ponies lived together in
the same paddock and were fed with grain and hay. There was no system in place
to check or control the feed. The PR submitted that the gardener may have
accidentally switched the feed buckets, resulting in the Horse unintentionally
ingesting the Prohibited Substance.
13. After reviewing the PR’s submissions and evidence, the FEI was satisfied that the PR
had established, on a balance of probabilities, that the source of the Prohibited
Substances was Regumate and Lexomil, which had been administered to the mare
at the Chateau where the Horse was staying. Lexomil contains Bromazepam, which
is the Prohibited Substance at issue in this matter. Therefore, the FEI considered
that the PR had established how the Prohibited Substances entered the Horse’s
body.
14. Furthermore, the FEI was satisfied that the PR had established, pursuant to Article
10.6 of the EAD Rules, that she bore “No Significant Fault or Negligence” for the EAD
Rule Violation1.
15. On 26 January 2026, the FEI notified the Tribunal that it had reached a settlement
of the dispute with the PR, which included the reduction of the period of Ineligibility
to be imposed on the PR.
16. On 2 February 2026, the Tribunal informed the Parties of the appointment of a one-
person hearing panel (the “Hearing Panel”) to adjudicate and approve this case. The
Parties were asked to provide any objections to the constitution of the Hearing
Panel by 5 February 2026.
17. On 3 February 2026, the FEI confirmed having no objection to the constitution of
1 Paragraphs 2.4 to 2.16 of the Settlement Agreement dated 21 January 2026 between the FEI and the PR together with the
Exhibits referenced therein evaluate the PR’s level of Fault and Negligence for the EAD Rule Violation.
4

the Hearing Panel.
18. The PR did not submit any objection to the constitution of the Hearing Panel.
IV. Accepted Terms
19. The Settlement Agreement is made in accordance with Article 10.8.2 of the EAD
Rules and is subject to the approval of the Tribunal.
20. The PR explicitly admitted the EAD Rule Violation and accepted the following terms
(the “Accepted Terms”) in accordance with Article 10.8.2 of the EAD Rules:
a) The PR admits the violation of Article 2.1 of the EAD Rules (The presence of a
Banned Substance and/or its Metabolites or Markers in a Horse’s Sample).
b) The PR established on a balance of probabilities how Bromazepam entered
the Horse’s system.
c) The PR bears No Significant Fault or Negligence for the EAD Rule Violation,
in accordance with article 10.6 of the EAD Rules.
d) The applicable period of Ineligibility is eighteen (18) months, in accordance
with article 10.6.2 of the EAD Rules, commencing as at the date of this Final
Decision (the Provisional Suspension already served will be credited against
the imposed period of Ineligibility).
e) The FEI Lifetime Measuring Certificate received at the Event is invalidated.
f) The PR will pay a fine of 500 CHF.
g) Each party will bear its own legal and other costs incurred in connection with
these proceedings.
h) No other Sanctions will apply in this case.
i) The EAD Rule Violation is considered a prior violation for the purpose of
Multiple Violations in accordance with Article 10.9.2 of the EAD Rules.
V. Decision
21. The Tribunal has jurisdiction over this matter pursuant to Article 38 of the Statutes,
Article 159 of the GRs, the EAD Rules, the VRs and Article 18 of the IRs. The PR is a
member of the FRA-NF, which is a member of the FEI. The PR is therefore bound by
the EAD Rules.
22. Having reviewed the case summary, the full reasoning of the Settlement Agreement
5

and the Accepted Terms, the Hearing Panel takes note that the FEI has agreed that
the PR established, on a balance of probabilities, how Bromazepam entered the
Horse’s system.
23. The Hearing Panel further acknowledges that the PR and the FEI have agreed on
the terms to conclude these proceedings, in accordance with Article 10.8.2 of the
EAD Rules, as detailed under Section IV of this Final Decision.
24. The Hearing Panel confirms that the Accepted Terms of the Settlement Agreement
comply with the EAD Rules and finds no grounds to object to them.
25. In particular, the Hearing Panel notes that, in view of the Settlement Agreement
reached by the parties that the PR bears No Significant Fault or Negligence for the
EAD Rule Violation, the period of Ineligibility imposed on the PR is reduced to a
period of eighteen months, starting as at the date of the Provisional Suspension.
26. Therefore, and in accordance with the mutual consent of the Parties, the Hearing
Panel hereby directs the Parties to fully comply with all the terms of the Settlement
Agreement. Furthermore, this Final Decision concludes this case, C26-0002
MANDILLE, 2025/BS06 GABOR DE FLORYS.
27. The Parties acknowledge and agree that pursuant to Article 13.3 of the EAD Rules,
this Final Decision will be made public by the FEI. The terms set out in the Settlement
Agreement are a full and final settlement of all claims relating to the subject matter
of these proceedings.
28. The Settlement Agreement and this Final Decision are not subject to appeal under
Article 12 of the EAD Rules.
DECISION TO BE FORWARDED TO:
a. The Parties: Yes
b. The Secretary General of the NF of the person sanctioned: Yes
c. Any other: No
FOR THE FEI TRIBUNAL
_______________________________________________
Ms Harveen Thauli, One-Member Panel
